9. Recovering a representation from its Ptolemy coordinates
We now show that a Ptolemy assignment on K determines a generically decorated boundary-
unipotent representation, which is given explicitly in terms of the Ptolemy coordinates. The idea is
that a Ptolemy assignment canonically determines a (G, N)-cocycle on M.

equations. The latter were invented by Thurston [27] to explicitly compute the hyperbolic structure
(and its deformations) of a triangulated hyperbolic manifold, and used eﬀectively in [22, 17, 9].
The gluing equations make sense for any 3-cycle.
